title: Release 3.0.0 obligations
description: What the published contract owes at the major bump, and the followers a bump stales.
desiredOutcome: Every promise COMPATIBILITY.md dated to this release is delivered in code, and the document records it as delivered rather than pending.

tasks.title: The deprecation the contract dated to this release is delivered
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: a tests.add entry naming no file is a FINDING for a tdd task that is not done or cancelled, and the published contract records the deprecation as delivered rather than pending. COMPATIBILITY.md promises it in its own words - from 2.3.0 an entry naming no file is a warning whose text names the release the refusal arrives in, and at 3.0.0 it becomes a finding - and that document is a contract rather than a description, so shipping the major without it makes the document false. MEASURED BEFORE DECIDING: zero entries in this project's own plan and zero in the shipped example name no file, so the flip costs neither. The warning's text currently announces the future refusal; a finding announces nothing, it refuses, and the sentence has to change with it - including the pointer to the repair script, which is still the right advice for a plan written before the rule. The terminal and non-tdd exemptions stay exactly as they are: a settled task's tests.add is a record of work already judged.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__manifest_phases.py: a tests.add entry naming no file on a live tdd task is a finding, while the terminal and non-tdd exemptions stay silent

outcome.technical: The unnamed tests.add entry is appended to findings rather than warnings for a graded task, the announcing clause is removed from its text and from three documents that repeated it, and repair-tests-add.py excludes this rule's own finding from the two validator gates that would otherwise stop it repairing the entries it exists for.
outcome.descriptive: The deprecation the contract dated to this release refuses instead of warning, and the script that repairs it still runs.

tasks.title: The browser fixture and the reason table it derives from disagree
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: npx vitest run is green, and whichever side was wrong is the side that moved. RELEASE BLOCKER, found by the first full verify.sh --release. tools/ui-tests/gate-reasons.test.mjs seeds the out-of-policy tiers with NO values and expects the reason table to publish exactly one template taking none; the table publishes two, one carrying a file name and one carrying two numbers, so the fixture throws. The two landed in the same commit and have never agreed, which means this has been red since it was written and nothing ran it: the JavaScript tests run in CI and in the full verify only, never in the selftest sweep, so three days of work passed over them. ESTABLISH WHICH SIDE IS WRONG BEFORE CHANGING EITHER. The fixture's own comment argues that one tier is reached down both arms so asking with no numbers is a legitimate request for the other sentence - which reads as a model where values means NUMBERS and the file-name arm takes none. The helper that counts conversions counts both spellings, which contradicts that model. Decide whether the counter should distinguish a numeric conversion from a string one, or whether the fixture should seed the file name, and say which reading the hook's own writer supports - it is the writer that decides, not the fixture. ALSO WORTH SAYING IN THE REPAIR: the new refusal the plan gate gained for a tree it cannot place is not in the published table at all, and that table's own comment says a published set that quietly stops covering its subject is the defect it exists to prevent.

outcome.technical: The fixture seeds the file-name arm with a value, reconstructs both conversion spellings when it unfills, and matches the derivation's current wording; require-plan.py gained a comment naming why the cannot-place refusal is outside the published table, with the existing floor case as the enforcement.
outcome.descriptive: The browser fixture reads the arity model the writer actually uses, so the suite that grades a committed image is green for the right reason.
